First, notice that $△ABC$ is an equilateral triangle. Consequently, all of the interior angles must be equal to ${60}^{∘}:$ 

$$
m∠A=m∠B=m∠ABC={60}^{∘}
$$

Also, since $△CDB$ is an isosceles triangle, the base angles must have equal measure:

$$
m∠CBD=m∠D
$$

Notice also that $∠ACB$ and $∠DCB$ are supplementary, therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠ACB+m∠DCB & ={180}^{∘} \\ {60}^{∘}+m∠DCB & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠DCB & ={120}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

 Finally, we calculate $m∠D$ using the fact that the interior angles of a triangle sum to ${180}^{∘}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠D+m∠DCB+m∠CBD & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠D+{120}^{∘}+m∠D & ={180}^{∘} \\ 2m∠D & ={60}^{∘} \\ m∠D & ={30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$
